postings.title: Sales Compensation Manager
postings.text: Overview: The Sales Compensation Manager (L6) leads complex compensation operations workstreams that drive reliability, scalability, and risk reduction across the sales compensation function. You will own end-to-end commission administration for a large payee portfolio, ensuring flawless execution across payroll submissions, SOX compliance, exception management, and stakeholder delivery, operating at the frontier of what AI and modern tooling make possible so that automation is embedded by default, not bolted on. Operating with a 6–12 month horizon, you’ll independently scope and solve moderately complex problems, influence Directors and Sr. Directors, and raise the bar for the team through mentorship, enablement, and operational discipline with strong automation. The impact you will have: Own end-to-end sales compensation administration for a large payee portfolio with full accountability for accuracy, timeliness, SOX compliance, and high-quality execution across participant setup, plan distribution, calculation, payment readiness, and payroll submission. Lead payroll submission for one or more GEOs with 100% accuracy, timeliness, and SOX compliance, including zero-pay confirmations, audit checkpoints, and evidence completeness across controls. Proactively detect anomalies and apply conservative holds to prevent overpayment; operationalise Exception Committee items with traceable implementation and reduced exception cycle time, leveraging AI-powered anomaly detection and predictive payment risk scoring to identify issues before they reach payroll. Validate data across source-of-truth systems (Xactly, SFDC, HRIS, Anaplan, etc.), investigate issues such as incorrect credits, quota misalignments, and payout exceptions, and deliver actionable recommendations to leadership, deploying agentic validation workflows and LLM-based solutions to reduce manual reconciliation and improve decision quality. Lead large or moderately ambiguous projects independently, balancing multiple priorities, defining clear ownership across contributors, and creating repeatable inspection mechanisms (dashboards, check-ins, trackers) that consistently deliver outcomes on time. Influence business partners across Sales Ops, Rev Ops, Payroll, HR, Legal, Accounting, Finance, etc. by framing decisions in terms of field experience, risk, and audit compliance, acting as the trusted first point of contact in escalation paths. Own and advance the team’s automation roadmap, driving adoption of AI across commission operations workflows, including intelligent anomaly detection, AI-assisted exception triage, automated evidence generation, and agentic validation of data across source systems, identifying where AI creates real leverage and building repeatable operating rhythms, standardized SOPs, and audit-ready documentation that improve quality, speed, and consistency while reducing execution risk. Enable the team through templates, playbooks, evidence packs, and exception trackers, mentoring analysts (including offshore resources) to raise execution quality beyond individual scope. What we look for: 10+ years of end-to-end sales compensation administration and commissions system operations, spanning payroll submissions, SOX control operations, exception modelling/recalcs, and stakeholder deliverables. Advanced proficiency with Xactly (administration, configuration, reporting, troubleshooting) and Excel/Google Workspace for complex modelling, analysis, and insight generation. Strong data validation skills across source-of-truth systems (SFDC, HRIS, Anaplan, etc.) with demonstrated ability to detect anomalies, perform complex commission modelling, and translate findings into clear recommendations. Demonstrated program management experience across payroll and compliance/exception workflows, able to set and run cadences, produce audit evidence packs, define escalation paths, and maintain continuous audit readiness. postings.text: (P-1174) We are hiring a Senior Staff Software Engineer for Databricks' Engineering team reporting to an Engineering Leader. You will be part of the Databricks engineering organization, working with teams that develop Databricks products and features for thousands of enterprises worldwide. Key Characteristics As an executive engineering individual contributor at Databricks, you will have full ownership of the product or infrastructure direction in a major area, driving it from initial development to scalable solutions with clear business impact. You will serve as a force multiplier by elevating stability, reliability, and organizational processes, while bringing deep expertise in large-scale distributed systems. You will mentor senior engineers, contribute to recruiting, and lead high-impact company projects, often tackling complex problems beyond their comfort zone. Job Description At Databricks, we are obsessed with enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems, from security threat detection to cancer drug development. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform, so our customers can focus on the high value challenges that are central to their own missions. Our engineering teams build highly technical products that fulfill real, important needs in the world. We develop and operate one of the largest scale software platforms. The fleet consists of millions of virtual machines, generating terabytes of logs and processing exabytes of data per day. At our scale, we regularly observe cloud hardware, network, and operating system faults, and our software must gracefully shield our customers from any of the above. The Impact you will have: Solve real business needs at large scale by applying your software engineering. Deliver a highly scalable, available, and fault-tolerant engine processing hundreds of TB of data daily across thousands of customers Low level systems debugging, performance measurement & optimization on large production clusters. Build architecture design, influence product roadmap, and take ownership and responsibility over new projects Use your deep experience to help prevent and investigate production issues. Plan and lead complicated technical projects that work with several teams within the company. A strong influencer or driver in the organization’s roadmap and direction. Lead a TLG or similar review committee, or initiate and sustain an org/eng-wide initiative driven by engineering needs. Break down complex problems quickly into potential solutions, knowns, and unknowns, and de-risk (through prototyping/validation). Contribute as a Technical Team Lead by mentoring others, lead sprint planning, delegating work and assignments to team members and participate in project planning. What we look for: 15+ years industry experience building and supporting large-scale distributed systems. Comfortable working towards a multi-year vision with incremental deliverables. Motivated by delivering customer value and impact. Strong foundation in algorithms and data structures and their real-world use cases. Experience driving company initiatives towards customer satisfaction. About Databricks Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents. Headquartered in San Francisco with 30+ offices around the globe, Databricks offers a unified platform that includes Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse, and Unity Catalog. To learn more, follow Databricks on LinkedIn , X , YouTube , and Instagram . Benefits At Databricks, we strive to provide comprehensive benefits and perks that meet the needs of all of our employees. postings.text: RDQ427R146 At Databricks, we are building the platform for the next generation of AI-built applications, where developers can go from idea to production using AI coding agents and app-building platforms. We partner with the leading tools developers use to generate, build, and deploy applications, connecting them directly to Databricks data, AI, and application infrastructure. With Databricks Apps and Lakebase, developers can build with their preferred code-gen tools and deploy secure, data-driven applications directly on Databricks. These partnerships are critical to making Databricks a core platform for the rapidly growing ecosystem of AI-generated applications. Founded in 2013 by the original creators of Apache Spark, Databricks has grown from a tiny corner office in Berkeley, CA to a global organization with over 8,000 employees. Thousands of organizations, from small startups to Fortune 100, trust Databricks with their mission-critical workloads, making us one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies in the world and one of the top 5 move valuable private companies. More about the Team As the Sr. Technology Partner Director, AI Code-gen & Apps, you will be responsible for recruiting, developing, managing, and scaling our global partner ecosystem that makes Databricks the best place to build and run AI-generated applications. You will build and own strategic partnerships with leading AI coding agents, app builders, and developer platforms, creating deep product integrations, joint solutions, and GTM plays that connect these ecosystems to Databricks Apps, Lakebase, and the broader Databricks platform. We are looking for someone with experience building and scaling strategic partnerships across AI code-gen, app-building, or developer tool ecosystems, with a strong track record of driving product integrations, joint GTM, and partner-led growth. The role requires strong technical and GTM acumen, with the ability to work across Product, Engineering, Sales, and Marketing to drive integrations, joint solutions, and go-to-market execution. Success requires deep expertise in large-scale technology ecosystems, strong communication and prioritization skills, and a scrappy, entrepreneurial mindset to build partnerships that establish Databricks as the best place to run transactional database workloads. The impact you will have Build and own partnership strategies for a portfolio of leading AI coding agents and app builders, spanning product integrations, joint solutions, GTM, and marketing initiatives that drive measurable customer adoption and business impact. Lead strategic partnerships from opportunity identification and joint product planning through launch and scale, working closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, and Marketing to bring integrations to market and drive adoption. Drive enablement and field readiness to ensure both Databricks and partner teams can effectively position and deliver these joint offerings. Serve as the internal voice of top partners in category, collaborating with Product, Sales, and Marketing leadership to influence our roadmap and ensure our strategy addresses the evolving needs of the Developer Tooling & Database Ecosystem landscape. What we look for 7+ years of experience in product partnerships, business development, or partner management, including 3+ years working across AI code-gen, app-building, or developer tool ecosystems. Proven track record of launching strategic ISV integrations and joint GTM motions with leading developer platforms, AI code-gen companies, or hyperscalers. Deep understanding and network across Developer Tool & Database ecosystem — Postgres (big plus), Developer Marketplaces, next-gen Platform-as-a-Services, AI Coding, and CI/CD workflows, and ability to develop joint value propositions that resonate with technical and business decision-makers alike. Strong cross-functional leadership skills — able to influence Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, and Business Operations

This is a high-impact role focused on positioning our Security solutions (Cloud SIEM, Cloud Workload Security, CSPM, and more) into new and existing customers—expanding our footprint and helping customers modernize their security stack in the cloud. At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them. What You’ll Do: Act as the subject matter expert (SME) for Datadog Security products across a targeted account patch Collaborate closely with Enterprise AEs to support net new logo acquisition and expansion in strategic accounts Own and drive the security sales cycle from discovery to technical close, working closely with Sales Engineers Evangelize Datadog’s security story to security leaders (CISO, Security Architects, SecOps) Work cross-functionally with Datadog's partner, channel, and alliance teams to drive joint go-to-market motions Co-sell effectively with AEs and partners, contributing to deal strategy, solution alignment, and stakeholder engagement Stay informed on security trends and competitive offerings to differentiate Datadog Who You Are: Proven success selling into security buyers (CISO, SecOps, GRC, etc.) Experience co-selling in a matrixed environment, supporting or partnering with AEs and cross-functional teams Strong understanding of the partner/channel sales model, including how to navigate and influence joint selling motions Familiarity with modern security solutions such as SIEM, CSPM, CWPP, container/Kubernetes security Ability to build strong relationships with internal stakeholders, partners, and customer technical teams Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply. Benefits and Growth: High income earning opportunities based on self performance New hire stock equity (RSU) and employee stock purchase plan (ESPP) Continuous professional development, product training, and career pathing Sales training in MEDDIC and Command of the Message Intra-departmental mentor and buddy program for in-house networking An inclusive company culture, opportunity to join our Community Guilds Generous and competitive medical benefits package Retirement savings match Pet adoption and insurance program Benefits and Growth listed above may vary based on the country of your employment and the nature of your employment with Datadog. #LI-Hybrid Datadog offers a competitive salary and equity package, and may include variable compensation. Actual compensation is based on factors such as the candidate's skills, qualifications, and experience. In addition, Datadog offers a wide range of best in class, comprehensive and inclusive employee benefits for this role including healthcare, dental, parental planning, and mental health benefits, a 401(k) plan and match, paid time off, fitness reimbursements, and a discounted employee stock purchase plan. The reasonably estimated yearly salary for this role at Datadog is: $124,000 — $165,000 USD About Datadog: Datadog is the leading observability and security platform for the AI era, providing businesses with unified visibility across the technology stack to manage complexity at scale. postings.title: Senior Technology Partner Manager
postings.text: About the Role Datadog’s Technology Partnerships team builds and scales partnerships with the technology companies that matter most to our customers from AI/ML platforms to data platform providers. As a Technology Partner Manager, you will own the full, 360-degree relationship with a portfolio of strategic Technology Partners, with a particular focus on cutting-edge AI/ML and Data Platform companies. You’ll be the connective tissue across three pillars of partnership: co-build (joint product and integration roadmaps), co-market (joint awareness and demand generation), and co-sell (joint pipeline and revenue). This is a highly cross-functional, relationship-driven role that requires equal comfort in a product roadmap discussion, a marketing planning session, and a sales enablement meeting. At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds, and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them. What You’ll Do 360° Relationship Ownership: Own the end-to-end partner relationship for a portfolio of AI/ML and Data Platform technology partners, serving as the primary point of contact and trusted advisor across product, engineering, marketing, and sales stakeholders on both sides. Co-Build: Partner closely with Datadog Product and Engineering teams to identify, prioritize, and drive joint integration roadmaps; ensure integrations are built, launched, and continuously improved to meet customer needs. Co-Market: Design and execute joint marketing programs including webinars, blog posts, customer case studies, launch campaigns, and event collaboration with Datadog product marketing and partner marketing teams to build awareness and demand for joint solutions. Co-Sell: Build and execute go-to-market and co-sell plans with Datadog channel team, partner field and sales teams; enable Datadog’s global sales organization and partner sellers on joint value propositions, use cases, and co-sell motions to drive pipeline and revenue. Program Management: Track partnership commitments, joint business plans, and success metrics across the co-build, co-market, and co-sell pillars; report regularly to leadership on partnership health, pipeline, and revenue impact. Cross-Functional Orchestration: Act as the connective tissue between partners and internal Datadog teams including Product, Engineering, Marketing, Sales, and Channels & Alliances to keep joint initiatives moving and unblock issues quickly. Marketplace & Routes to Market: Ensure Datadog integrations are well-represented in partner marketplaces and directories, and identify new routes to market with partners, including joint listings on cloud and partner marketplaces. Enablement: Create and maintain internal and partner-facing content including playbooks, battlecards, and training that helps both organizations clearly articulate the joint value proposition. Market Awareness: Track trends across the AI/ML and data platform ecosystems to identify new partnership opportunities and ensure Datadog’s partner strategy stays ahead of a fast-moving market. Who You Are Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Business, or a related field; an MBA is a strong plus. 7+ years of experience in technology partnerships, alliances, partner management, or business development at a software, cloud, or SaaS company. Experience managing the full partnership lifecycle including technical/product collaboration, marketing programs, and sales/co-sell motions Comfortable working with technical products; able to understand integration architectures and translate them into clear business value for marketing and sales audiences. Familiarity with the AI/ML and/or data platform ecosystem (e.g., LLM providers, vector databases, data warehouses, data pipeline and orchestration tools) Proven ability to build trusted relationships with external partners and internal stakeholders across Prod

postings.title: Senior People Business Partner
postings.text: Datadog is seeking a Senior People Business Partner to work closely with business leadership and our People team to sit in our São Paulo office and help support our growing Go-to-Market (GTM) team in Latin America. This person will work closely to support the specific needs of our team members across the region while working strategically on People programs and initiatives. This is Datadog’s first PBP based in LATAM, so you'll be the primary People contact on the ground for the region. Datadog has had exponential growth year-over-year and has no plans to stop - there is a lot to learn from and contribute to our rapidly scaling team. At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them. What You’ll Do: Act as the sole in-region PBP in LATAM and provide on-the-ground support; represent our global PBP team to partner on the front line with employees and leadership across the region Advise, coach, and influence leadership on all things people-related, including: performance management, coaching, career pathing, employee relations, compensation, organizational development & scaling, training, culture, inclusion, employee engagement Partner remotely with departmental PBPs, COE teams, and People leadership, bridging global programs with local needs across time zones Consult with the appropriate People Center of Excellence (COE) team to gather their expertise and provide input on program design to enhance the employee experience Build, advise and consult on People policies, guidelines, and programs, in collaboration with COE colleagues Provide analysis and consulting to leadership to drive data-driven people decisions and implementation of best practices Assess employee development needs, make recommendations, and implement appropriate solutions aligned with the organization’s broader strategy Handle complex global employee relations issues, working with leadership to implement best practices and approach Who You Are: Experienced in 8+ years as an HRBP or in a related global HR role, preferably with experience in fast-growing technology companies Able to adapt your approach and pivot your skillset from strategic, high level program implementation to granular day-to-day needs of a fast paced business Experienced operating as a sole or lead People partner for a region or business, comfortable working without a local People team around you Comfortable with ambiguity and an evolving remit. You build structure where none exists and adjust as priorities shift Strong in your analytical & reporting skills; solid experience with HRIS (Workday is a bonus!) Experienced in working across business functions from first line to senior leadership; GTM business partnership experience strongly preferred A master in your project management and organizational skills, with a proven ability to design clear processes, and a detail-oriented yet flexible approach to problem solving Experienced in employee relations and knowledge of global employment practices Clear, direct, approachable, and friendly communication style and strong customer service orientation Strong interpersonal and communication skills and able to build relationships and trust at all levels of the organization Business level Portuguese and English fluency required; Business-level Spanish fluency strongly preferred Datadog values people from all walks of life. postings.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Storage Execution
postings.text: MongoDB powers mission‑critical workloads for customers who expect their data to be durable, highly available, and fast to access. The Storage Execution team builds the core infrastructure that makes those guarantees real. We are hiring a Senior Engineering Manager to manage the largely New York-based Storage Execution team. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is obsessed with customer success, takes the responsibility of durably storing customer data seriously, and has strong empathy for both their team and our users. This role can be based remotely in the United States. About the Storage Execution team The Storage Execution team sits at the heart of MongoDB’s Online Transaction Processing (OLTP) team. We own the core transactional read/write path on each node, across both today’s storage engine and a next‑generation cloud-native storage architecture. Our work determines how correct and performant MongoDB is for customers running mission-critical production workloads. The team’s responsibilities include: Defining and maintaining the internal collection and index APIs used by Replication, Query and Catalog modules, and commands for local reads and writes, plus the transaction and durability primitives that govern visibility, conflict resolution and crash recovery Integrating the next generation of MongoDB’s storage architecture into the server in a way that is predictable for other teams, scales with cloud elasticity, and preserves the performance and safety of the classic configuration Improving transaction processing speed and semantics of both single shard and cross-shard transactions Owning index builds and schema‑level storage operations (build/rebuild, cleanup, resumability) and ensuring they behave well for large, highly available clusters running write-heavy workloads Building validation, diagnostics, and storage‑focused test infrastructure to catch durability issues early and keep the system trustworthy at scale Partnering with neighboring teams on flow control, prioritization and load-shedding to stay within resource limits, protecting durability and availability at the cluster level without starving critical operations What you’ll do Lead, grow and manage a New York–based team of 8 to 10 engineers; ensure clear expectations, high standards, and healthy, sustainable execution Own the team’s roadmap across durability, availability, performance, and developer productivity, in partnership with OLTP leadership and Product Management Manage customer escalations involving storage behavior and durability; work directly with Support, Atlas, and other server teams to reproduce, root‑cause, and resolve issues Drive process and tooling improvements that raise engineering velocity and code quality (e.g., ownership, review expectations, customer escalation and build failure practices) Partner closely with Replication, Query, Sharding, Catalog & Routing, Storage Engines, and Atlas teams on cross‑team features such as the new storage architecture, availability improvements, and workload management Represent Storage Execution in planning, staffing, and calibration; make thoughtful tradeoffs between near‑term deliverables, longer‑term availability gaps, and platform investments Candidate profile 8+ years building, debugging, and tuning distributed and/or highly concurrent systems software (databases, storage engines, filesystems, or similar) 2+ years managing engineers directly, including hiring, performance management, and coaching across a range of levels Willing to work East Coast hours Strong proficiency in at least one compiled, statically-typed language such as C++, Rust, or Go; postings.title: Senior Software Engineer
postings.text: The database market is massive and MongoDB is at the head of its disruption. At MongoDB we are transforming industries and empowering developers to build amazing apps that people use every day. We are the leading modern data platform and the first database provider to IPO in over 20 years. Join our team and be at the forefront of innovation and creativity. The MongoDB Cloud Services Team is a diverse group of contributors working together to help our users manage MongoDB at global scale. The Cloud Team is responsible for MongoDB Atlas: our database as a service offering, and fastest growing product, which allows users to deploy fault-tolerant, globally distributed MongoDB clusters in just minutes. The Backup Team delivers essential infrastructure to help our customers in their hour of need - providing the ability to quickly restore a massive, distributed database to any point in time at the click of a button. The Backup Team’s mission is to make MongoDB backup more reliable, faster, and also cheaper. This team is responsible for the Backup Agent (Go), the extensive server-side infrastructure (Java) which manages 100s of TB of data and processes billions of operations per day, and the user interface (Javascript) that customers use to manage their backups. Common project themes are performance, scaling, and ease of use. We are looking to speak to candidates who are based in New York City for our hybrid working model. We're looking for someone who is Skilled at writing large-scale, distributed backend systems in a compiled language (Java, C#, Go, etc.) Fond of chasing down tough problems in a distributed systems environment Cool under pressure - has wrangled production crises, and secretly finds this a little fun Experienced with Linux, and able to correlate application performance problems with underlying hardware limits Comfortable working across the stack of a modern web application Always striving to expand their knowledge Curious, collaborative and intellectually honest Responsibilities Work closely with product teams, considering the user’s perspective while helping the team achieve success Collaborate with team members over best practices and core concepts Hold yourself accountable to your actions, maintaining the balance between accomplishing goals with research & development Own our core values and adhere to them in your work, and Stay up to date with best practices in web engineering Success Measures A Software Engineer will be successful in this role when they Are open, honest and willing to contribute and collaborate with others Develop confidence in finding their way across the platform Can take responsibility for the planning and execution of a major feature, representing Engineering when working with Product and Design Are willing to learn and contribute to all parts of the stack Are resolute in their approach to problem solving, balancing the needs of their team with the willingness to get to the bottom of issues About MongoDB MongoDB is built for change, empowering our customers and our people to innovate at the speed of the market. postings.title: Digital Adoption & Lifecycle Manager
postings.text: About Mixpanel Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at mixpanel.com . About the Customer Digital Experience Team Customer Digital Experience sits within Customer Engineering, the technical arm of Mixpanel's Customer organization. Our sharpest focus is the digital-only segment: thousands of companies with no proactive account coverage. Some have technical resources available to them, but that support is entirely reactive. It answers the ticket and solves the problem in front of it. Nobody is watching for the customer who implemented and then never built a report, or the account whose usage has been sliding for a month. Our job is to be proactive,, and everything we build should be as automated as possible, without a human initiating it. Our programs run across the full customer base and are not one-size-fits-all. We build flows that branch and adapt by segment, tuning the content, timing, and channel for who's receiving them. An onboarding flow for a digital-only customer carries the whole experience; the version reaching an account with a dedicated team is tuned to complement what that team is already doing. Same underlying program, deliberately different execution, continuously optimized based on what each segment responds to. We're close to the data and to the technical reality of how customers implement and use Mixpanel. We're not guessing at what customers are doing; we can see it, and we build against it. This is a small, new team standing up a new function. The playbook isn't written yet; we're writing it together. About the Role As our Digital Adoption & Lifecycle Manager, you'll own the communications that drive adoption, retention, and expansion across Mixpanel's customer base, with our digital-only customers as the sharpest test of whether the programs work. You'll design lifecycle programs triggered by real behavior: a team that just implemented but hasn't built their first report, an account whose query volume dropped for three straight weeks, a power user hitting the edge of their current plan. Then you'll write the emails and in-product messages that move them forward. This is a builder's role, not a maintainer's role. You'll define the segmentation, write the copy, set up the triggers, instrument the measurement, and then argue with the data about what to change. It's also a deeply collaborative one. You'll work hand in hand with our Customer Success Digital Programs Manager, sharing a roadmap and dividing the work. You'll partner with Marketing on the overall email calendar so our lifecycle sends and their campaigns aren't competing for the same inbox. You'll support adoption initiatives coming out of Product, turning a launch into something customers actually try. And you'll take cues from customer-facing teams about what's landing and what isn't. Very little of this job happens alone. You'll also help define what agentic customer success looks like at Mixpanel. The scaled programs we build today are rules and triggers; the ones we build next will involve AI agents that can interpret a customer's situation, decide what that customer needs, and act. We're early here and we don't have the answers. We want someone who is already experimenting, who already has opinions about where agents help and where they break trust, and who wants to shape how this gets built. If you like clean handoffs and finished systems, this isn't it. If you want to build the thing from zero and own the number it moves, read on. postings.title: Senior Data Scientist, AI Product Insights
postings.text: About Mixpanel Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at mixpanel.com . About the Team The Proactive Insights team is a newly formed team at the center of Mixpanel's AI-first analytics vision. With a greenfield charter, we're building the intelligent layer that transforms Mixpanel from a tool you query into a partner that works for you. We answer the question every data-driven team asks: "What changed, why, and what should I do about it?" We proactively keep users informed about what matters in their data, delivering the right insights and recommendations at the right time, to the right places, both inside and outside of Mixpanel. Some examples of what we are building: Signals : Statistical analysis that automatically identifies which user behaviors cause downstream business outcomes — such as which actions genuinely improve 30-day retention — using causal inference to move beyond correlation Forecasting : Time-series modeling that projects whether a KPI (e.g. Signups) will hit its goal by end of quarter — including trend decomposition, seasonality adjustment, and confidence bands against a target. Simulation : Causal impact modeling that estimates how moving one metric (e.g. weekly sharing rate) by a given amount will ripple through to downstream KPIs like retention or revenue — giving teams a quantified basis for prioritization Cohort Detection : Automated identification of at-risk user cohorts by finding active users who resemble known churned segments across both behavioral patterns and descriptive characteristics, before they churn. Offline batch survival analysis models that estimate each user's probability of a future outcome (e.g. likelihood to churn or convert within 30 days). About the Role As the first Data Scientist embedded in product engineering, you'll champion integrating cutting-edge data science techniques into Mixpanel's products and serve as a methodological resource for cross-functional teams tackling problems that benefit from deeper DS expertise — such as adaptive experimentation. You won't just advise on Proactive Insights; you'll be the analytical brain driving how Signals, Forecasting, Simulation, Predictions, and Cohort Detection actually work. Your models are the reasoning layer behind an AI system that proactively tells customers what changed, why, and what to do next — and increasingly, the layer behind an agent that acts on their behalf. As more of this experience becomes agentic, rigorous causal grounding is what separates a trustworthy recommendation from a plausible-sounding one. You'll be the person who makes sure it's the former. You'll design and validate causal inference approaches that go beyond surface-level correlation, and partner on how those outputs get translated — often via LLMs — into clear, natural-language, actionable experiences for Mixpanel's customers: you own the rigor, the system owns the explanation. You'll partner closely with strong product engineers who own the implementation — your job is to make sure the methodology is rigorous, well-documented, and grounded in real outcomes. You'll also collaborate cross-functionally with teams like AI platform, analysis, and data infrastructure to scale your analytic solutions beyond what you could build alone. This is a high-impact, high-autonomy role on a small, fast-moving team. You'll have significant influence over the analytical direction of a new product category at Mixpanel that helps thousands of companies understand what truly drives their most important metrics. ABOUT THE TEAM Strategic Finance is where Snowflake's biggest financial questions get answered: what an acquisition is worth, where the company lands over the long term, what our EPS looks like, and how much capital each entity needs. Our work doesn't end at the model — we translate what the numbers say into clear points of view that help the CFO and senior leadership act. ABOUT THE ROLE This is a high-visibility role spanning corporate development, long-term planning, and technical accounting — a combination that's rare for a single analyst seat. You will build serious financial models and provide real decision-driving support to the executive level. This role is best suited for candidates from investment banking, private equity, or FP&A who are ready to work across M&A diligence, forecasting, and EPS simultaneously. You will work closely with a Senior Manager who owns methodology and will teach it. WHAT YOU WILL DO Financial Storytelling Turn model output into a clear narrative for executive and board audiences — the headline, the key drivers, and the recommendation. Build exec summaries, ELT slides, and briefing memos where every number is defensible, and present your analysis directly to senior finance leadership. M&A Diligence and Deal Modeling Dive into target financials to understand unit economics, cost structure, and the operating model. Build acquisition models under the direction of the deal lead: standalone and pro forma projections, purchase price allocation, accretion/dilution, and sensitivity cases framed around what has to be true for the deal to work. Long-Term Planning and 3-Statement Forecasting Maintain and extend the total-company long-term model — full P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow — driven off bookings, revenue, headcount, and cost-per-head. Run scenarios and translate trade-offs into terms leadership can act on: growth versus margin, hiring pace versus operating leverage. SBC and EPS Modeling Run the monthly stock-based compensation forecast, including grant-level expense attribution, new-grant and refresh assumptions, and forfeitures by function and legal entity. Build quarterly and annual basic and diluted EPS forecasts using treasury stock method mechanics and share count roll-forward. Entity-Level Cash Flow and Capital Planning Build entity-level cash flow forecasts to size capital requirements and funding needs across international subsidiaries. Support Tax on transfer pricing analytics and convert entity-level detail into a plain funding recommendation: which entities need cash, how much, and when. WHAT YOU WILL NEED • 1–3 years of experience in investment banking, private equity, corporate development, transaction advisory, or corporate FP&A • Ability to build or work extensively in a 3-statement operating model, and explain how the balance sheet and cash flow tie • Familiarity with M&A modeling mechanics — accretion/dilution, purchase accounting, sources and uses • Advanced Excel with disciplined model structure and a bias toward auditability over cleverness • Strong written and verbal communication — able to take a complex analysis and land it in three sentences and one slide • Solid GAAP fundamentals with genuine interest in SBC (ASC 718) and EPS (ASC 260) • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accountin

postings.text: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. About the team Abuse Research Group (ARG) handles proactive threat hunting and adversary behavior analysis across Stripe products. Rather than reacting to alerts, the team maps end-to-end fraud and abuse paths, validates novel attack vectors, and identifies product conditions that enable fraud. Using agentic automated testing and simulation tools, ARG translates research into actionable threat advisories, strategic control recommendations, and regression scenarios to systematically eliminate vulnerabilities. What you’ll do As an Abuse Research Engineer in the Abuse Research Group, you will play a critical role in safeguarding Stripe’s financial ecosystem by proactively hunting for advanced threats, dissecting complex fraud vectors, and extracting actionable adversary intelligence. Rather than relying solely on reactive alerts, you will develop and execute hypothesis-driven threat hunting operations across internal telemetry and external sources to uncover fraudulent tools, tactics, and techniques (TTPs) before they impact Stripe’s platform. Central to this work is FT3 (Fraud Taxonomy 3.0), Stripe’s multi-layered taxonomy that decomposes monolithic fraud into structured kill chains. Collaborating cross-functionally with Fraud Ops, Strategy, Risk, Onboarding, and Security, you will integrate threat intelligence, build agentic simulation workflows, and systematically eliminate product vulnerabilities. Responsibilities Proactive Threat Hunting & Kill Chain Analysis: Formulate hypotheses and conduct iterative threat hunting operations across Stripe systems and external data. FT3 Taxonomy: Apply and enrich the FT3 framework across empirical datasets and incidents, standardizing threat intelligence across kill chain phases and targeted API endpoints. Threat Intelligence & Signal Expansion: Partner with teams like Fraud Intelligence to integrate, curate, and automate threat feeds into engineering workflows. Cross-Functional Advisories & Strategic Controls: Translate raw research and retrospective findings into actionable threat advisories and control recommendations (policy, technical systems, support workflows, and detection mechanisms) for stakeholders across Fraud, Risk, Onboarding, and Security. Agentic Testing & Adversary Simulation: Utilize agentic automated testing frameworks to simulate adversary TTPs, validate whether deployed controls interrupt empirical kill chains, and generate regression scenarios to exercise controls. Who you are We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. Minimum requirements 5+ years of experience conducting threat intelligence, threat hunting, or technical incident response within cyber security, product abuse, or trust domains. 5+ years of experience analyzing large, complex datasets using data analytics tools to identify anomalies, map behavioral trends, and solve complex fraud problems. B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Expert proficiency in Python and SQL, with demonstrated experience using code and scripting to automate workflows, build investigative tools, or query big data pipelines. Hands-on experience in log analysis (e.g., application logs, API route telemetry, network security events), digital forensics, and cyber investigation method

Site Reliability Engineers (SREs) at Braze are responsible for keeping all internal-facing services and platforms running smoothly, ensuring consistent system reliability and maximum infrastructure uptime. SREs blend the roles of sensible system administrators and software engineers, applying sound engineering principles, operational discipline, and mature automation to our production environments. We specialize in distributed systems, operating at an extraordinary scale that includes serving over 3.3 billion monthly active users, collecting hundreds of billions of data points each month, and delivering billions of messages to our customers' end-users daily. This Senior SRE role is specifically focused on supporting the Braze Ruby on Rails monolith and our growing fleet of Go API services. This position is embedded with product engineering teams who own APIs, taking their high-level feature requirements and helping translate them into reliable, highly scalable technology stacks. You will be responsible for the ingress fleets and API ingestion layers which serve as the main entry point for how the entire internet talks to Braze. Because of the highly operational and foundational nature of these ingress fleets, a deep, hands-on experience of both NGINX and Kubernetes is important. postings.text: At Braze, we have found our people. We’re a genuinely approachable, exceptionally kind, and intensely passionate crew. If Braze sounds like a place where you can thrive, we can’t wait to meet you. We're looking for a technical writer to join our Tech Writing team — someone who thinks in systems as naturally as they think in sentences. At Braze, documentation is infrastructure: a connected, structured body of knowledge that both developers and machines read from, not a collection of individual pages. You'll spend as much time shaping how that knowledge is organized and generated as you will writing it. Our documentation practice is already well established, with a mature style guide, writers who own specific product domains, and a workflow where AI-assisted drafting sits alongside traditional technical writing. Your job is to push it forward on two fronts. The first is architectural: defining the metadata, taxonomy, and context our tooling relies on to produce useful first drafts. The second is editorial: becoming a genuine expert on Braze's platform and bringing the kind of scrutiny that turns a plausible draft into documentation our customers can actually trust — accurate, well-structured, and consistent in voice with every other Braze experience. WHAT YOU’LL DO Define and maintain the metadata (YAML front matter), taxonomy, and contextual guidelines that our AI-assisted drafting workflows depend on Review and verify machine-generated prose and code samples line by line, checking technical accuracy, edge-case behavior, and voice before anything ships Write and revise API references, integration guides, and conceptual documentation in our docs-as-code environment, owning feature updates end to end Become an expert on the Braze platform, distilling complex functionality into approachable, user-centric language Help oversee and maintain the documentation GitHub repository Work closely with Product Management, Engineering, Support, Customer Success, Marketing, and Implementation teams to pin down how the platform actually behaves and to validate real customer integration paths Organize content so it serves a developer mid-integration and a system retrieving context — the same structure has to work for both Ensure documentation applies voice, style, and branding consistent with other client experiences Keep improving our documentation and client education experience through feedback-gathering, research, experimentation, and data-driven decisions Promote and foster knowledge exchange across teams WHO YOU ARE 3+ years writing documentation for genuinely technical audiences — APIs, SDKs, or developer platforms — with writing samples that show both range and precision Fluent in information architecture and knowledge management A rigorous editor with a sharp instinct for the draft that reads well but says something subtly wrong Comfortable with Git, Markdown, YAML, and docs-as-code workflows An active, practical user of LLMs and AI tooling in your own work — you've figured out where they help and where they don't Able to explain technical concepts to engineers and to non-technical readers

Our Applied AI Architects are forward-deployed practitioners who combine domain judgment with hands-on build capability: they embed with business teams, treat employees as users and workflows as product surfaces, and ship working agents on shared infrastructure. The function runs in two tracks. GTM Architects are permanently embedded in the GTM organization, each owning a portion of a customer and prospect lifecycle that spans Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, and Support; when they address friction in one stage, they work the surrounding levers holistically, mapping how those functions connect today and how AI could connect them better. G&A Architects rotate across corporate functions like Finance, People, Legal, and Operations, driving each cohort to self-sufficiency. You will lead this team. That means defining how a new role category operates, owning the portfolio of engagements across the business, and answering for the outcomes: adoption that persists, workflows that measurably improve, and committed bets that read out in business metrics like sales ramp time, quota capacity, and competitive win rate. This is a player-coach role. You will carry enough build and field surface yourself to keep your judgment current, while your primary output is the team: who they are, where they embed, what they ship, and whether it works. You inherit the hiring manager seat for all Architect roles, a unified interview loop, and an operating model with real momentum. What the function becomes from there is yours to shape, in close partnership with our Director of Applied AI Product, the CIO and CTO organizations, and the leaders of the functions your team serves. What You'll Do Build the team. Close the open Architect reqs across both tracks (GTM and G&A), then own onboarding, development, and performance for a team of senior, highly autonomous ICs operating in a role category that barely exists in the market. Define what good looks like and what the career path is. Own the engagement portfolio. Decide where Architects embed, what they prioritize, and when they rotate or scale back. Balance permanent GTM surface ownership against rotational G&A engagements. Say no to good ideas so the team ships great ones. Answer for the bets. Own delivery and measurement of the committed GTM bets (sales ramp time, quota capacity / customer-facing time, competitive win rate) and run the promotion pipeline for G&A candidate bets. Every bet pairs a business outcome with leading indicators; you keep both honest. Run the operating discipline. Enforce the engagement lifecycle (discovery, prioritization, readout, design, build, deliver, monitor) and the cohort maturity model. Adoption is the bar: an ignored output is a bug, and your team operates what it ships until it is productized. Stay hands-on. Review agent designs, specs, and output

You’ll define what “correct” looks like, run our calibration and adjudication program, and build ongoing training that measurably improves decision quality. Translate supply chain business requirements into a prioritized technology roadmap, working across internal teams and vendor partners to sequence and deliver. postings.title: Sr. Product Quality Engineer
postings.text: Sr. Product Quality Engineer ABOUT THE ROLE As a Senior Product Quality Engineer at Peloton, you will be responsible for ensuring our hardware products are designed, manufactured, and tested to a high quality standard so that our members can continue to access Peloton’s fitness experiences throughout the life of their products. You will need to identify major risks starting from the earliest project stages and define quality plans to mitigate and control these risks prior to launch. You will also be responsible for leading investigations of top issues from root cause analysis through to corrective action, and documenting learnings to prevent recurrence of similar issues in the future. This role will work closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Service and Repair, and other teams starting from concept through to mass production and sustaining. YOUR DAILY IMPACT AT PELOTON Partner with multi-functional teams through early risk assessments (using FMEA/NUD processes and past lessons learned). Implement mitigation strategies and test plans to address and close potential risks. Drive alignment across the various Quality functions, including Supplier Quality, Field Quality, Reliability, Failure Analysis, and Safety. Lead cross-functional response to critical quality escalations and drive complex issues to closure using methodical 8D/RCCA approaches. Define, implement, and audit quality processes at our FATP sites to ensure final products meet quality targets. Develop predictive models to estimate warranty rates from available field test and reliability data. Communicate Quality risks, mitigations, and next steps to the leadership team and other key stakeholders. Influence partners to implement quality improvements for field performance. This role requires domestic and international travel up to 30%. YOU BRING TO PELOTON Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Science, or other technical discipline. 6+ years of experience in product development with 3+ years specifically in a Quality role for complex electro-mechanical products (e.g., Fitness Equipment, Medical Devices, Automotive, or Consumer Electronics). Demonstrated understanding of NPI (New Product Introduction) cycles and how to successfully drive quality improvements during development. Track record of leading cross-functional technical teams through the resolution of business-critical quality issues. Ability to develop specifications and test plans, and translate test results into field predictions. Proficiency in statistical data analysis and related software tools (e.g., Minitab, JMP). Deep technical knowledge of advanced quality tools and methodologies (eg., DOE, MSA, Hypothesis testing, GR&R, CpK). Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a proven ability to build consensus and influence decisions at all levels of an organization. BONUS QUALIFICATIONS Advanced Degree in Science or Engineering. Operational Leadership & Lifecycle Management: Manage the end-to-end network project lifecycle—from traffic shaping and SD-WAN optimization to establishing SOPs, security policies (with InfoSec), and handling Tier-3 disaster recovery. postings.title: Staff Tooling Engineer
postings.text: Staff Tooling Engineer About the Role The Staff Tooling Engineer is responsible for leading and optimizing tooling development from initial tooling design through mass production sustaining with ODMs (Original Design Manufacturers) and CMs (Contract Manufacturers). This role plays a critical part in ensuring that tooling design meets strict quality, throughput, and cost targets while driving Design for Manufacturing (DFM) and Design for Assembly (DFA) in close collaboration with internal Mechanical Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain teams. The ideal candidate possesses deep hands-on expertise in plastic injection molding, sheet metal stamping, die casting, hydroforming, and tooling fabrication processes, along with proven cross-functional communication and supplier management skills. Your Daily Impact at Peloton DFM & Engineering Collaboration: Collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams (ME, ID, Hardware, Quality) to conduct robust DFM/DFA reviews, guiding process selection, material selection, and tooling qualification plans. Tooling Design & Validation: Lead technical reviews for tooling designs, mold layouts, and drawings (including Moldflow simulation, gate placement, cooling, parting lines, and ejector pin layouts). Validate tooling designs with suppliers and toolmakers to proactively troubleshoot issues. NPI Execution: Drive tooling deliverables across all Hardware Product Development phases (Alpha, EVT, DVT, PVT) to support key NPI programs, ensuring timely OK2TOOL and OK2FAB approvals. Supplier & ODM/CM Management: Work closely with ODMs and CMs to manage tooling build progress, trial runs (T1/T2), root cause troubleshooting, and yield improvements on the manufacturing floor. Maintenance & Tooling Audits: Establish and maintain supplier-facing tooling maintenance standards and asset management procedures. Conduct on-site supplier and tooling audits to ensure quality maintenance and mold longevity. PPAP & Quality Alignment: Partner with Quality and Supplier Quality Engineering (SQE) teams to establish SOPs for part inspection, technical support for PPAP (Production Part Approval Process), and dimensional/cosmetic qualification. Cost & Capacity Optimization: Assist in building simulation models for tooling and part cost analysis ("should cost"), evaluating factory capacity/capability, and driving continuous improvement initiatives for tooling cost reduction and cycle time optimization. You Bring to Peloton Education: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Tooling Engineering, or equivalent practical experience. Experience: 8+ years of hands-on engineering experience in plastic injection molding, die casting, sheet metal stamping/bending, and tooling fabrication within a high-volume manufacturing environment. Technical Expertise: In-depth knowledge of tool design, tool steel selection, mold/die fabrication, heat treatment, and post-processing (e.g., CNC machining, deburring, plating, surface finishing). Proficiency in 3D CAD modeling (SolidWorks, Creo, or AutoCAD) and simulation software (e.g., Moldflow, CAE tooling analysis). Strong familiarity with DFM/DFA principles, GD&T, engineering drawings, and quality management frameworks (PPAP, ISO/IATF 16949). Problem Solving: Strong analytical and root cause analysis skills (e.g., 8D, DOE, Kaizen, SPC). Communication: Excellent written and oral English communication skills for effective collaboration with cross-functional global teams and international suppliers. Travel: Ability to travel up to 30% to manufacturing facilities and supplier locations as needed. You will define direction across multiple streams (transactional, context-driven, lifecycle, loyalty, promo) before anything gets built, and you connect the loyalty calendar to the broader marketing calendar so every touchpoint compounds to maximize customer and business impact. Sequence loyalty mechanics against the marketing calendar so menu drops, brand moments, and new restaurant openings each land with loyalty-specific value behind them. Evolve offer logic and discount governance in partnership with Finance, optimizing who, what, when, why, and how much to maximize the ROI of every discount dollar and continually strengthen the SG Rewards program economics. CRM and Lifecycle Define what each owned channel is for, how messages sequence across a member's journey, and how frequency is governed across the base. Set audience and segmentation strategy grounded in behavior, and refine journeys continuously to eliminate friction in the customer experience. Develop SGs personalization approach across the customer journey in partnership with Product. Lead strategy and concept for lifecycle programs (onboarding, frequency building, deceleration and win-back, tier progression) before execution begins. Own the martech roadmap and vendor strategy, including requirements for future capability needs like decisioning and personalization. Report performance in terms of incremental behavior, incremental revenue, and ROI, and translate it into recommendations that shape decisions beyond marketing. Team and operating model Hire, develop, and retain a high-performing team; set clear expectations and grow people into their next role. Steward how the team works cross-functionally: intake, prioritization, briefing standards, QA, and campaign velocity. When you join Sweetgreen, you not only invest in your own future but help create spaces where food, people, and purpose come together. postings.title: Associate Business Development Consultant — Workplace Advisory
postings.text: Create world-class workplaces as you build your business development career. As an associate business development consultant at Gallup, you will gain expertise in consultative sales, consulting frameworks and account leadership. Working with high-achieving coworkers and experts, you’ll unlock your individual talents and develop knowledge, skills and expertise on workplace dynamics and issues. Your bold thinking, effective communication, commitment to excellence and inspiring influence will lead to lasting change for organisations. You’ll begin your career at Gallup by getting to know our business and clients as you support business pursuits and projects. postings.title: Director — Talent Assessment Science
postings.text: Set the direction and shape the science behind who gets hired. At Gallup, our pre-hire assessment science is backed by decades of research, millions of data points and a body of work that has influenced how organizations select talent around the world. We are looking for a director to lead the next chapter of that science in close partnership with the researchers, technologists and client teams who carry it to market. The work of our Hiring Analytics practice spans the full range, from building proprietary instruments to curating and validating the best of what already exists. Leading this practice requires exceptional judgment to choose the right solution and strategic vision to modernize and advance assessment science in a rapidly evolving industry. This is a player-coach role in the truest sense: senior enough to set where the portfolio goes, yet close enough to the methods that the work still carries your fingerprints. You will guide the practice into adaptive testing, AI-augmented assessment and modern validation while developing a small, senior team that grows because you are in the work alongside them. What You’ll Do Lead the construction and validation of assessments from the ground up across cognitive, behavioral, situational and work-sample formats: item writing at scale; scale development; IRT calibration; and the criterion, content and construct validation that hold up to EEOC and Uniform Guidelines scrutiny. Partner directly with clients , scoping needs, shaping solutions, presenting psychometric findings and defending the science with equal fluency to legal teams, executives and non-technical stakeholders. Build structured interview systems at speed, developing behaviorally anchored, job-relevant guides that balance scientific rigor against commercial timelines — two demands that rarely agree — so clients have tools they can actually use. Draw discoveries out of our data , mining Gallup’s 17M+ pre-hire assessment dataset for novel validity evidence, performance predictors, subgroup patterns and insights that serve clients and advance the field, including the occasional inconvenient result. Advance the methodology in CAT, IRT, AI-assisted item generation, automated scoring, and candidate evaluation models; connect that science to CliftonStrengths ® and the talent philosophy the firm is built on; and serve as the authoritative voice on AI in assessment and where its fast-moving regulation is heading. Develop your people through real reps on real problems. Set the scientific standard; coach researchers and psychometricians on method and craft; and guide the assessment science on major client engagements alongside strategy, analytics, technology and client-service colleagues. What Makes You Stand Out Validation rigor across the full arc: You have done confirmatory factor analysis for construct validity, criterion-related designs that predict rather than merely correlate, norming and standardization, and adverse impact analysis that you have taken through to remediation. A researcher’s instinct for discovery: You treat a dataset as territory to explore rather than merely validate, alongside fluency in AI as both tool and context, building with it and thinking ahead about what it means for the integrity and fairness of hiring decisions. Assessment science expertise: You have deep knowledge of EEOC regulations, the Uniform Guidelines and SIOP principles, and you have confidently defended assessment methodologies to legal stakeholders and regulatory audiences. The temperament of a player-coach: You are senior enough to set the standard, secure enough to stay in the craft, and willing to tell a room of executives something it would rather not hear. Your credibility comes from your science, not your title. What You Need — Requirements A Ph.D. in I-O psychology or a closely related field At least 10 years of experience building assessments for clients, on commercial timelines, that businesses paid for and used, with at leas

postings.title: Quality Engineer
postings.text: Build quality into every product and help shape the future of AI-powered software. As a quality engineer at Gallup, you'll help deliver software our clients can trust by partnering with product managers, software engineers, designers and fellow quality engineers to ensure quality in every stage of the software development life cycle. Rather than simply executing test cases, you'll apply systems thinking to identify risks, develop thoughtful validation strategies and help ensure every release delivers an exceptional customer experience. As Gallup continues to expand its AI-powered products, you'll also have opportunities to contribute to testing intelligent workflows and emerging AI capabilities. What You’ll Do Develop a deep understanding of product features, customer workflows, system interactions, APIs, data flows, integrations and technical dependencies to identify quality risks and determine the most effective validation strategy Collaborate within Gallup's Product Operating Model alongside product managers, software engineers, designers and fellow quality engineers to ensure quality in every stage of product development Design, execute and maintain manual and automated tests across user interfaces, APIs, integrations and end-to-end workflows Develop and maintain automated test suites using Playwright or comparable modern automation frameworks Perform exploratory, regression, smoke and end-to-end testing to uncover system risks and validate critical customer experiences Integrate automated tests into CI/CD pipelines to provide fast, reliable feedback throughout development Troubleshoot automation failures and partner with engineering teams to improve test stability, reliability and automation coverage Create and maintain test plans and traceability that reflect product intent, customer impact and overall validation strategy Support production validation and investigate customer-reported issues when needed Continuously improve quality engineering practices, automation capabilities and release confidence What Makes You Stand Out Systems thinking: You naturally connect product features, APIs, integrations and customer workflows to identify risks before they become production issues. Quality-first mindset: You view quality engineering as an integral part of software development and proactively build quality into products rather than testing only at the end. Automation expertise: You develop maintainable, scalable automated testing solutions that improve release confidence and accelerate delivery. Collaborative partnerships: You build strong relationships across Product, Engineering and Design teams, communicating effectively to solve complex problems and improve outcomes. Continuous learning: You embrace emerging technologies, modern testing approaches and AI-enabled engineering practices while continually expanding your technical expertise. What You Need Bachelor's degree in computer science, computer engineering, information systems or a related field, or equivalent professional experience required At least three years of experience in quality engineering, including both functional and automated testing, required Experience testing web applications and REST APIs required Experience developing automated tests using Playwright, Cypress, Selenium or comparable automation frameworks required Experience working within Agile software development teams required Familiarity with Git and CI/CD pipelines required Experience using test management platforms such as QMetry, Azure DevOps Test Plans or TestRail required Experience with TypeScript/JavaScript and/or Python preferred Experience with SQL and database validation preferred Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS or Azure preferred Experience with performance, security or data quality testing preferred Experience contributing to automation frameworks and reusable testing utilities preferred Experience testing AI-powered applications, chatbots, copilots or intelligent workflow

postings.title: Director, Lifecycle Marketing Operations
postings.text: About the role Chime is hiring a Director of Lifecycle Marketing Operations to build and run the operational engine behind everything we send to members: campaign execution, channel health and deliverability, the automation and platform layer, and the governance that keeps it all safe and high quality at scale. Most of that work is manual today. Your mandate is to make it faster, higher quality, and increasingly automated, with an agent-supported operation as the destination. You'll lead a growing execution team through an execution lead and a set of channel and platform specialists, and partner closely with MarTech, Growth Engineering, and the lifecycle strategy leads to turn strategy into live, high-quality messaging. This is a leadership role with real technical depth: you set the operational strategy and prioritize the work, and you go deep into the detail when it counts. In this role, you can expect to Own the Messaging Operations engine and set its operational strategy across campaign execution, channel health, deliverability, automation, and the platform layer — and own the metrics that say whether it's working: throughput, quality, speed to launch, deliverability, and channel health. Own the operational process end to end, from intake to launch: build, QA, deployment, and the standards that keep quality and speed high as volume grows. Drive the automation and AI-agent roadmap, taking the team from manual execution to supervising and governing automated workflows, and fold what you learn from experimentation into the wider Lifecycle roadmap. Own governance for everything that ships: channel standards, deliverability and compliance, and the QA model for automated and agent-driven sending, in a regulated environment where safe sending is non-negotiable. Own channel excellence across email, push, in-app, and SMS — health, analytics, opt-in/opt-out, and deliverability. Set the benchmarks the operation runs on, connect them to the business metrics leaders care about, and scout and pilot new channels before we need them. Build and lead a growing, increasingly technical team through an execution lead plus channel and platform specialists: set the structure, proactively source talent for your team and across Chime, set clear expectations, and give the team the context and room to own outcomes. Act as Lifecycle's primary stakeholder to MarTech on how we use the platform and what gets built on top of it, partner with Growth Engineering on the build, and work with the lifecycle strategy leads to turn their plans into live messaging. To thrive in this role, you have 8+ years in marketing or CRM operations, lifecycle execution, or martech, including 3+ years leading teams — with experience developing leads or managers, not only individual contributors. Deep expertise with engagement and CRM platforms (Braze or similar): campaign operations, journey architecture, automation, and the technical layer underneath. A strong track record in governance: setting and enforcing channel, deliverability, and compliance standards, and building the QA that keeps a high-volume operation safe. A real track record of building toward automation. You've scaled manual processes and have a clear point of view on where AI and agents fit in marketing operations. Deep channel health and deliverability expertise at scale: sender reputation, inbox placement, fatigue management, and opt-in/opt-out hygiene. Strong operational and analytical judgment. You run on metrics, can tell at a glance whether the engine is healthy, and balance speed against safe, compliant sending in a regulated environment. The influence to align peer Directors and VPs across Marketing, Engineering, and Product on shared standards, and the range to lead at altitude on strategy and transformation while translating the technical detail into a story each audience can act on. Bonus points if you have Experience standing up or scaling an automation or agent layer in a marketing or CRM context

This role is embedded directly within the cross-functional Chime Enterprise growth effort and operates as the growth owner, not just a marketing advisor. You'll sit at the intersection of growth strategy, experimentation, performance analysis, and product marketing craft: identifying opportunities, prioritizing and running experiments, and driving metric movement against clear goals. In this role, you can expect to Growth Ownership & Strategy Own end-to-end growth strategy and outcomes for Chime Enterprise's employee-side funnel, from opportunity sizing through roadmap delivery against quarterly and annual goals. Our mission is to enforce Plaid's privacy commitments and regulatory obligations in the systems themselves rather than in policy documents: we build the platform and controls that govern how data flows through Plaid — where it lives, who can use it, for what purpose, and for how long. That includes verifiable deletion of consumer data on request, enforcement of data-use restrictions so downstream systems can only use data in permitted ways, and the cataloging and classification that let Plaid know what data it holds and how sensitive it is. As a Staff Software Engineer on Data Governance, you will set the technical direction for how Plaid enforces data governance at scale. You'll lead the design of distributed backend systems that reliably delete, restrict, and track data across dozens of services, making architectural decisions whose blast radius spans the whole company. You'll drive multi-quarter initiatives from ambiguous privacy and regulatory requirements through to shipped, auditable infrastructure — decomposing the hard problems, aligning multiple engineering teams behind a plan, and staying hands-on in the code for the highest-risk pieces. You'll be a force multiplier: raising the technical bar through design reviews and mentorship, and partnering deeply with Legal, Privacy, Security, and product-engineering teams to turn obligations into controls the rest of the company can build on. You will serve as the bridge between business strategy and technical execution, partnering directly with Product, Engineering, Clinical, and Operations leaders to solve complex infrastructure challenges and ensure seamless, sustainable data flows across provider-facing systems. postings.text: Clover Health is investing in our fraud detection and investigation capabilities and is seeking a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations to join our Legal department as a senior individual contributor. That might mean writing a script to automate repetitive work, pulling apart a dataset when a standard report falls short, or working with an LLM until it produces something genuinely useful—all with the goal of finding smarter, more effective ways to investigate potential provider fraud. As a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations, you will: Build Your Own Investigative Tooling: Use AI to write the queries, scripts, and prompts that turn millions of claim lines and/or medical record data into a prioritized list of leads. Develop investigative plans, gather and analyze evidence (including claims data and medical records), and reach well-supported conclusions. Use LLMs and analytics to compress the parts of an investigation that have always been slow — reading unstructured data, triaging grievance narratives, and sizing exposure. Build Defensible Documentation: Develop case files and memos that are factually complete, well-organized, and prepared with the evidentiary and procedural standards necessary for downstream enforcement, recoveries, or provider actions. Collaborate Across Functions: Work with Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, provider relations, revenue operations, and SIU teams to gather information, validate findings, and translate investigative outcomes into operational improvements, provider education, and member impact. Success in this role looks like: In your first 90 days , you have embedded yourself as a trusted partner to both the Legal department and Clover’s SIU.
