postings.title: Senior Product and Design Strategist
postings.text: Omada Health is on a mission to bend the curve of chronic disease. Job overview: A Product + Design Strategist can carry a problem from an ambiguous user and business opportunity to a validated experience. As a Product + Design Strategist, you will operate at a senior IC level: leading the highest-leverage, most ambiguous scopes of work at Omada and setting direction for a collection of related experiences rather than a single feature. You translate engineering’s increased pace into more of the right experiences launched for our customers and members, not just more output. AI is a core part of how this role works day to day as a co-intelligent partner you direct across research synthesis, prototyping, spec drafting, and analysis, extending your judgment so you can move from open question to validated direction faster, with more rigor. You thrive in ambiguity, especially in 0 to 1 spaces where the problem is not yet defined and the path forward is yours to shape. You bring a strong, evidence-backed point of view, initiative and ability to find answers, and you're as comfortable in an executive strategy conversation as you are prototyping with users. Core Responsibilities A Product + Design Strategist owns four things — problem framing, direction setting, vision casting, and alignment. Everything else is craft in service of these. Problem framing — turning ambiguous asks, business opportunities, and lived member experience into a scoped, evidence-backed understanding of what's actually wrong and worth solving. Problem framing & requirements — turning a vague ask into a scoped, buildable piece of work. User journey mapping — diagnosing end-to-end friction and drop-off with empathy. Research study design & execution — running interviews, surveys, and experiments to test assumptions. Data analysis (quant + qual) — pulling product performance data and synthesizing qualitative signal into a clear read of the problem. Competitive, inspiration, & analogous research — auditing adjacent products for pattern or gap insight. Metrics instrumentation — in partnership with data analytics, defining upfront what “solved” will actually look like. Direction setting — reconciling research, data, engineering, and business input into a clear point of view on what to pursue, and revisiting that call against real evidence once it's live. Synthesis & direction-setting — recommending which directions to pursue and which to drop. Prioritization & trade-offs — arbitrating competing product and stakeholder requests with transparent rationale. Quantitative and qualitative evaluation design & analysis — defining core questions and hypotheses, then translating results into insights and go/no-go decisions. Stop/start/continue investment decisions — revisiting prior bets against evidence of what's actually working. Vendor & partner evaluations — build vs. buy justifications. Vision casting — making the future state tangible and compelling enough that cross-functional partners, leadership, and members can see it and support it. Roadmap ownership & narrative — owning a multi-quarter roadmap that maps to corporate OKRs, key strategic initiatives, operational cadences, and commercial cycles. Executive communications & narratives — building the strategic story for budget and prioritization conversations. Product marketing & commercial partnerships — carrying the vision into go-to-market and partner contexts. Visual & interaction design — makes the vision tangible enough to inform viability, desirability, and feasibility decisions, and to support build and operational planning. Job overview: Omada is seeking a Senior Director, Capacity Planning, Workforce Operations & Analytics to lead all teams in this department as it scales into a world‑class, human‑led and AI‑enabled operations and analytics function that supports Omada’s multi‑condition platform across Health Coaching, Cardiometabolic Specialists, Physical Activity Specialists, Behavioral Health, Physical Therapy, Member Support, Member Navigation and Supply Chain. This leader will be accountable for end‑to‑end department strategy and execution, translating enterprise and care team goals into clear priorities and operating systems for workforce capacity planning, staffing operations, licensing and credential management, and care team analytics. Reporting to the VP Operational Excellence, the Senior Director will oversee the centralized department that supports care team capacity planning and staffing, including the administration of Omada’s third party licensing and credentialing software, and runs the care team analytics “spoke” within Omada’s hub‑and‑spoke analytics model. This role includes full department leadership: setting 1–3 year strategic priorities, controlling key cost of revenue and gross margin levers, and leading the adoption of AI-enabled predictive modeling and analytics to improve capacity planning, staffing efficiency, and decision-making across care teams. Your Impact: As Senior Director, Capacity Planning, Workforce Operations & Analytics, you will: Own the care teams Capacity Planning, Workforce Operations & Analytics operating vision and roadmap Define and maintain a clear operating vision for the department as the “operational brain and data engine” for care teams. Translate company and care teams strategies into a concrete 1–3 year departmental strategy covering capacity planning, workforce staffing operations, licensing and credential management, and care team analytics/AI enablement. Design and run the Capacity Planning, Workforce Operations & Analytics operating system Own and evolve the operating rhythms, standards, and visibility systems for the department (e.g., forecasting cadences, scheduling and intraday management, department business reviews, data mart and dashboard foundations). Create and maintain scalable rules for shrinkage, occupancy, and staffing allocation that reduce variation, enable predictable quality, and tie operational decisions directly to cost of revenue and gross margin outcomes. Lead and scale multi‑motion capacity planning and staffing operations Own capacity planning and staffing models that support Health Coaching, Cardiometabolic Specialists, Physical Activity Specialists, Behavioral Health, Member Support and Member Navigation, ensuring accurate, efficient coverage at sustainable cost‑to‑serve. Build out new capabilities including Physical Therapy state‑based capacity planning and staffing, integrating licensure and credential constraints into state‑level supply planning and staffing decisions. Lead Licensing and Credential Management for care teams and clinical staff Oversee system administration for a third party licensing and credentialing management system. Ensure credential status is accurate, compliant, and embedded into capacity and staffing decisions. Partner with Clinical, Legal/Compliance, and People teams to build workflows, controls, and data integrations that reduce regulatory risk while enabling flexible, efficient deployment of care team capacity across states. Own the short term and long term analytics roadmap with the Senior Leadership Team Lead care team analytics as an analytics “spoke,” elevating existing analytics into an AI‑enabled function that supports operational excellence, experimentation, and strategic decision making across all care teams. Want to help over two million people receive quality mental healthcare? Come join our mission of getting therapy in the hands of everyone! postings.title: Senior AI Engineer
postings.text: At Talkspace, we are committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, inclusive, and belonging-centered workplace where everyone can thrive while making a difference in mental health. Want to help over two million people receive quality mental healthcare? Come join our mission of getting therapy in the hands of everyone! We are looking for an experienced Senior AI Engineer to join our team. The Senior AI Engineer will be a pivotal technical leader, responsible for designing, building, and scaling the autonomous AI agents that form the core of our behavioral health platform. This role requires deep expertise in developing complex, multi-agent systems, leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) for reasoning, planning, and goal setting, and applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) techniques to model and influence human behavior safely and ethically. You will drive the entire lifecycle of our agents—from developing cognitive architectures and interaction models to ensuring their robust, high-availability deployment and continuous learning in a production environment. Given the sensitivity of behavioral health, this role demands an exceptional focus on safety, ethical autonomy, transparency, and data privacy. The ideal candidate is a seasoned engineer who can bridge the gap between theoretical AI (specifically RL and planning) and real-world, scalable, and impactful user interactions. To work at Talkspace, you need to be as passionate as we are about our work, and excited to partner with us on delivering quality mental healthcare. Talkspace HQ is in NYC; this position is based in Eastern Standard Time hours. What You’ll Do Autonomous System Architecture: Design and implement the technical architecture for Tee's core AI agents, including the development of planning modules, memory/retrieval systems, goal-setting algorithms, and tool-use orchestration. Reinforcement Learning (RL) for Behavior: Apply advanced RL, Inverse RL, or related control theory methods to develop agents capable of adaptive, long-term intervention strategies that maximize positive user outcomes while minimizing risk (e.g., optimizing interaction sequencing, timing, and content). LLM Integration and Fine-tuning: Select, fine-tune, and deploy foundation models (LLMs) to power agent reasoning, natural language understanding, and empathetic, context-aware communication with users. Complex Interaction Modeling: Develop models for human-agent interaction (HAI), incorporating principles from cognitive science and behavioral economics to ensure agents are effective, trustworthy, and aligned with therapeutic protocols. Simulated Environments: Construct robust simulation environments for pre-training and testing agent policies, ensuring system stability and safety across a wide range of psychological and behavioral scenarios. Performance and Resilience: Optimize the deployment environment to manage the computational demands of multi-agent orchestration, ensuring low-latency decision-making and high system resilience. Technical Strategy: Lead the evaluation and adoption of new agentic frameworks, reasoning technologies, and system design patterns that position Tee as a leader in autonomous behavioral health technology. Agent Evaluation & Observability: Design and implement comprehensive evaluation pipelines for multi-agent orchestration—including visualisations, trace-level analysis of LLM calls and tool invocations, offline evaluation against golden datasets, real-time production monitoring for behavioral drift and outcome correlation, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop annotation workflows. Establish metrics frameworks to assess reasoning quality, task completion, safety compliance, and task alignment across the full agent lifecycle. About You Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, or a highly quantitative field.
